concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
question: Which act was passed by the British Parliament to control the territories of the East India Company majorly in Bengal in the year 1773?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Regulating Act.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Regulating Act:-**

 
 
• The Regulating Act was passed by the British Parliament in 1773.
 
• **The Act was designed to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India and to curb its powers.**
 
• It was the first major intervention by the British government in the affairs of the East India Company and paved the way for further reforms and acts.
 
• The Act established a system of governance in India, with a Governor-General and a Supreme Council, and also introduced other reforms such as the establishment of a court of justice in Calcutta.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Government of India Act:-**

 
 
• The Government of India Act is a set of laws passed by the British Parliament between 1773 and 1935 to regulate the government of India.
 
• **The Government of India Act 1935 was a landmark piece of legislation that introduced a number of important constitutional reforms in India, including:**
 
 
• The establishment of a federal system of government, with a central government and provincial governments.
 
• The introduction of direct elections to the provincial legislatures.
 
• The expansion of the franchise to include more Indians.
 
• The creation of a Federal Court, with the power to adjudicate on disputes between the central government and the provincial governments.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act:-**
 
 
• The Indian Councils Act was a series of laws passed by the British Parliament between 1861 and 1909 to expand the size and functions of the legislative councils in British India.
 
• **These acts were introduced in response to growing demands for self-government from Indian nationalists.**
 
 
 
• **Charter Act:-**
 
 
• A Charter Act is a law passed by the British Parliament to renew the charter of the British East India Company, which was a private company that ruled British India on behalf of the British Crown.
 
• **The Charter Acts were passed every 20 years, and they regulated the company's trade and administrative powers.**
